content.value_statement: Teams need consistent .NET backend patterns for APIs, services, and data access. This skill provides practical templates and guidance for EF Core, Dapper, caching, testing, and resilience.
actual_capabilities: Guides .NET backend architecture with layering, modules, dependency injection, and service boundaries.
Provides service and repository templates for validation, result handling, caching, logging, and data access.
Explains EF Core performance patterns, including projections, eager loading, split queries, compiled queries, and transactions.
Explains Dapper patterns for connections, parameterized queries, mapping, transactions, TVPs, and cancellation tokens.
Covers unit and integration testing patterns for services, repositories, and API flows.
Calls out common anti-patterns such as blocking async code, early materialization, and string-concatenated SQL.
limitations: It does not execute, compile, or validate generated .NET code.
Project-specific security, schema, infrastructure, and performance choices still need expert review.
It focuses on backend C# and .NET work, not frontend UI development.
The included templates are examples, not complete production applications.

use_cases.title: Design a New API Service
use_cases.description: Apply clean architecture, dependency injection, async patterns, caching, and observability when building a new .NET API.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Data Access
use_cases.description: Compare repository, EF Core, and Dapper choices against documented performance, safety, and maintainability patterns.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Generation
use_cases.description: Steer Claude, Codex, or Claude Code toward consistent service, repository, testing, and resilience conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dotnet-backend-patterns to plan a small .NET service for this feature. Include layers, dependencies, validation, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Repository Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dotnet-backend-patterns to design repository access for this entity. Compare EF Core and Dapper choices for my workload.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Production Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for reliability and operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dotnet-backend-patterns to review this .NET API flow for caching, resilience, cancellation, logging, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize a Backend Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for refactoring an existing module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use dotnet-backend-patterns to refactor this backend module. Preserve behavior and explain changes for architecture, data access, and tests.

output_examples.input: Create a product service pattern for a .NET API.
output_examples.output: A concise service design with validation, result handling, repository calls, cache usage, logging, cancellation support, and focused test cases.

output_examples.input: Review my EF Core query performance.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering tracking mode, projection, includes, split queries, indexes, transactions, and measurable follow-up tests.

output_examples.input: Choose EF Core or Dapper for this endpoint.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary that weighs maintainability, query complexity, throughput, transaction needs, and team familiarity.

best_practices: Provide the target .NET version, architecture style, ORM choice, and database constraints before asking for implementation guidance.
Ask for a small implementation plan before generating large service, repository, or testing changes.
Validate generated output with builds, tests, profiling, and security review before production use.
anti_patterns: Using templates without adapting namespaces, domain models, database schema, and dependency registrations.
Requesting broad rewrites without specifying .NET version, ORM, architecture, and acceptance criteria.
Treating example snippets as production-ready without tests, monitoring, error handling, and environment validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build and review .NET backend APIs, services, repositories, tests, caching, and data-access patterns.

faq.question: Does it support EF Core and Dapper?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes separate guidance for EF Core best practices and Dapper query patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and templates that must be adapted, compiled, tested, and reviewed in your project.

faq.question: Is this only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. It can also guide refactoring, code review, performance tuning, and test planning for existing .NET backends.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. Generated code still needs project-specific security review, dependency review, and production validation.
